$comment: Copy of zipnative docs/data/errors.json (the frozen 39-code error vocabulary and 11 diagnostic codes, with raisedWhen/remedy per code) plus, per error code, the CLI mapping "cli": { code: E_*, exitCode } taken from src/utils/ziperr.ts (ZIP_TO_CLI), and, per diagnostic, "raisedBy": the CLI commands whose engine paths can emit it (batch surfaces whatever its tasks raise). The --json error envelope carries error.code (the E_* class) and error.zipCode (the ZIP_* cause, verbatim). tests/docs/consistency.test.ts enforces sync with the source table. cli.remedy (when present) is the CLI flag or command that lifts the refusal — the machine-actionable counterpart of the engine message, also emitted as error.remedy in the --json envelope (source: ZIP_REMEDY in src/utils/agent.ts).

errors.raisedWhen: An option value fails validation: compression.level outside 0-9, a non-positive chunkSize, or an argument shape the API forbids.
errors.remedy: Fix the option value at the call site — the message names the offending option and the accepted range.

errors.raisedWhen: The pure-TS deflate encoder received more than 2 GiB of input in one call.
errors.remedy: Split the input, or stream it entry by entry.

errors.raisedWhen: A named entry does not exist where one is required (readEntry, replaceEntry, removeEntry, renameEntry).
errors.remedy: Names are case-sensitive — iterate entries() to list what the archive holds.

errors.raisedWhen: A named entry already exists where absence is required (addEntry over an existing name; rename onto an existing name).
errors.remedy: Use replaceEntry() to overwrite, or removeEntry() the target first — renames never overwrite implicitly.

errors.raisedWhen: A usage contract was violated: toBytes() with addStream() entries, drain-order violations in forward iteration, single-shot data()/skip() reuse, push() after an inflator finished.
errors.remedy: The message names the contract and the compliant call sequence.

errors.raisedWhen: strict: true escalated the first conformance diagnostic of the operation into a thrown error.
errors.remedy: The message embeds the underlying diagnostic code; handle the archive shape it names, or drop strict and receive diagnostics via onDiagnostic.

cli.remedy: drop --strict, or fix the producer named by the diagnostic

errors.raisedWhen: An internal invariant broke — this is a zipnative bug, not an input problem.
errors.remedy: Report it with a reproduction archive or generator script.

errors.raisedWhen: The input is smaller than 22 bytes, no end-of-central-directory record exists in the trailing scan window, or no candidate is self-consistent (trailing garbage / hostile ambiguity — zipnative refuses to guess).
errors.remedy: The bytes are not a ZIP archive, are truncated, or carry trailing bytes — verify the source, or remove the trailing bytes if the archive is trusted.

errors.raisedWhen: The end-of-central-directory record contradicts the archive layout: entries-on-disk differs from the total, or the central directory overlaps the record itself.
errors.remedy: The archive is corrupt or hostile — re-obtain it from the source.

errors.raisedWhen: A zip64 sentinel is set but the zip64 end-of-central-directory locator is absent.
errors.remedy: The archive is truncated or corrupt — re-obtain it.

errors.raisedWhen: The zip64 end-of-central-directory record is not where the locator points (and not at the fallback position).
errors.remedy: Corrupt archive, or an unsupported prepended-data layout — rebuild the archive without the prefix.

errors.raisedWhen: The central-directory walk contradicts the declared counts or size: it ends early, a record extends past the declared size, or bytes remain beyond the declared entries.
errors.remedy: The archive is corrupt or hostile — re-obtain it from the source.

errors.raisedWhen: A fixed or variable-length ZIP record (EOCD, zip64 EOCD, central or local header) or an entry's payload overruns the available bytes.
errors.remedy: The archive is truncated — verify the transfer completed.

errors.raisedWhen: An expected PK signature is absent: no local file header at the offset the central directory declares, no EOCD signature at the resolved offset, or a forward stream that does not start with a local header.
errors.remedy: The archive is corrupt or the bytes are not a ZIP stream.

errors.raisedWhen: A forward byte stream ended mid-record or mid-entry (iterateZipEntries sources).
errors.remedy: The stream was cut — verify the producer sent the complete archive.

errors.raisedWhen: A 64-bit field exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2^53 - 1).
errors.remedy: Archives this large are not supported — the public API uses number, not bigint.

errors.raisedWhen: A writer-side entry name violates the name rules: empty, NUL bytes, backslashes, absolute paths, or '..' segments (zipnative never writes traversal-capable archives).
errors.remedy: Use relative, forward-slash paths without traversal segments.

cli.remedy: a plain relative name (no .., no drive, no device name)

errors.raisedWhen: Duplicate entry names where uniqueness is required: add() over an existing name, or opening a duplicate-name archive with createZipModifier().
errors.remedy: Every archive path must be unique; for duplicate-name source archives, extract and rebuild with createZip().

errors.raisedWhen: A deflate stream ends mid-block: the data ran out before the final block completed.
errors.remedy: The compressed payload is truncated — re-obtain the archive.

errors.raisedWhen: A deflate stream is structurally invalid: bad Huffman codes, invalid symbols, out-of-range back-references, LEN/NLEN mismatches, or an unsupported block type.
errors.remedy: The compressed payload is corrupt — re-obtain the archive.

errors.raisedWhen: Two entries share bytes: duplicate local-header offsets, an entry extending into another, or an entry claiming to start inside the central directory.
errors.remedy: Overlapping-entry archives are a decompression-bomb/smuggling shape and are always rejected — there is no opt-out.

errors.raisedWhen: A local file header contradicts the central directory on the compression method.
errors.remedy: Parser-differential archives are rejected — rebuild the archive with a sane tool.

errors.raisedWhen: A zip64 value contradicts a non-sentinel classic field (zip64 may only REPLACE sentinel fields).
errors.remedy: Parser-differential archives are rejected — rebuild the archive.

errors.raisedWhen: An entry name cannot be made safe: it escapes the extraction root (zip-slip — '..' segments, absolute paths, drive letters, UNC prefixes, backslash tricks, NTFS alternate data streams) or is a Windows reserved device name (CON, NUL, COM1..LPT9).
errors.remedy: The archive is hostile, corrupt, or POSIX-authored with device-name files; pass rejectTraversal: false to silently skip such entries instead (they are never emitted).

errors.raisedWhen: An entry is a Unix symlink and rejectSymlinks is on (the default).
errors.remedy: Pass rejectSymlinks: false to receive the link target as ordinary data (never materialized as a link).

errors.raisedWhen: Two entries resolve to the same output path under onDuplicate: 'error' (the default).
errors.remedy: Pass onDuplicate: 'first' or 'last' to resolve the shadowing deliberately.

errors.raisedWhen: Decompressed bytes fail the declared CRC-32 (central directory, local header, or data descriptor).
errors.remedy: The data is corrupt; expectedCrc/actualCrc carry both values. Pass verifyCrc: false only if you accept corrupt output.

errors.raisedWhen: Sizes contradict: the decompressed size differs from the declared size, or local-header sizes/CRC contradict the central directory.
errors.remedy: The archive metadata lies — treat the archive as corrupt or hostile.

errors.raisedWhen: Inflate produced more output than the declared or permitted bound.
errors.remedy: The archive metadata lies about this entry, or raise the relevant limit if the archive is trusted.

errors.raisedWhen: No data-descriptor form (signed/signless × 32/64-bit) matches the measured CRC and sizes of a bit-3 entry.
errors.remedy: The stream is corrupt or hostile — use openZip() on the complete archive for the authoritative view.

errors.raisedWhen: The active codec failed mid-decompression (corrupt payload surfaced through node:zlib, DecompressionStream, or an injected codec).
errors.remedy: The data is corrupt or hostile — the wrapped detail is in the message.

errors.raisedWhen: A configured security bound from ZipLimits was exceeded.
errors.remedy: Raise limits.<limit> explicitly if this archive is trusted — the message names the key and both values.

cli.remedy: --max-<bound> <size> (the bound is named in detail.limit; trusted input only)

errors.fields: limit (the offending key), configured = observed = NaN
errors.raisedWhen: The limits override itself is invalid: an unknown key, or a non-positive/NaN value.
errors.remedy: Fix the limits object at the call site — valid keys are listed in the message.

errors.raisedWhen: An entry is encrypted (ZipCrypto or strong encryption) — encryption is unsupported in 1.x by policy.
errors.remedy: Check entry.isEncrypted to route around such entries; encrypted entries remain copyable by the modifier without decompression.

errors.raisedWhen: An entry uses a compression method with no registered codec.
errors.remedy: registerCodec() one, or re-save the archive with store/deflate.

errors.raisedWhen: The archive is multi-disk/spanned (EOCD disk fields, zip64 locator disk count, or an entry starting on another disk).
errors.remedy: Multi-disk archives are an explicit anti-goal — rebuild as a single archive.

errors.raisedWhen: An addStream() entry exceeds 4 GiB (Zip64 streaming is not implemented yet).
errors.remedy: Buffer the content via add() or split it; a per-entry opt-in is tracked on the roadmap.

cli.remedy: create without --stream (buffered entries are fully Zip64)

errors.raisedWhen: Forward reading met a data-descriptor (bit 3) entry whose payload cannot be delimited without the central directory: store+bit3, encrypted+bit3, or a custom codec without consumed-byte reporting.
errors.remedy: Use openZip() on the complete archive instead.

cli.remedy: cat / extract on the complete file (random access)

errors.raisedWhen: A registered codec supports only the other access mode: stream-only codecs via readEntry(), or codecs without a streaming decompressor via readEntryStream().
errors.remedy: The message names the compliant call (readEntryStream() or readEntry()).

cli.remedy: cat / extract --codec <module> on the complete file

diagnostics.raisedWhen: Bytes precede the archive (self-extractor stub or concatenation); all offsets were shifted accordingly.
diagnostics.remedy: Verify the prefix is expected for this file.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: EOCD location on every random-access open (openZip); the forward reader (stream) never sees the EOCD.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: More than one end-of-central-directory signature exists; the last self-consistent candidate was used.
diagnostics.remedy: Expected for archives whose comment embeds the signature; otherwise inspect the file.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: EOCD location on every random-access open (openZip); an append-only modify output or a nested zip typically carries one.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A local header's filename bytes differ from the central directory's; the central directory wins.
diagnostics.remedy: Rebuild the archive with a sane tool if the divergence is unexpected.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: Read paths only (prepareRead): list and inspect never compare local-header names; modify raises it while verifying survivors or copying under --compact.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The 0x7075 Unicode Path extra field disagrees with the header name; the header name wins (0x7075 is never acted on).
diagnostics.remedy: None needed — informational about the producer's inconsistency.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: Flag bit 11 claims UTF-8 but the name bytes are invalid UTF-8; decoded as CP437 instead.
diagnostics.remedy: The producer lied about the encoding — verify names look right.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: Central-directory parse (every random-access reader) and the forward reader (stream, local headers).

diagnostics.raisedWhen: The central directory holds duplicate entry names; getEntry() returns the last.
diagnostics.remedy: Iterate entries() to see every duplicate; extraction under onDuplicate: 'error' throws.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: Name-keyed lookups only (the reader builds its name index): cat, inspect --entry, verify --entry. list, inspect and whole-archive verify iterate without it; inspect counts stats.duplicateNames and --check no-duplicates gates them.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An extra field overruns its declared length and was skipped.
diagnostics.remedy: None needed — the malformed field is ignored, the rest is parsed.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: A zip64 extra supplied a value for a non-sentinel classic field; the header value wins.

diagnostics.remedy: Pin a Date (or accept the DOS-epoch default) for deterministic bytes.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: --date now on create (also --parallel and batch --task create) and modify.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: Timestamps are pinned but a platform codec is in use — bytes are stable per environment, not across zlib builds.
diagnostics.remedy: Pass deterministic: true to pin the pure-TS encoder for cross-runtime identical bytes.
diagnostics.raisedByNote: create with a pinned --date <ISO> on a non-pure deflate tier without --deterministic (also --parallel and batch --task create); modify does not emit it.

diagnostics.raisedWhen: An incremental save() left more than 50% dead bytes; removed/replaced content remains recoverable in the file.
diagnostics.remedy: Use saveCompact() for true deletion and a canonical layout.

sink.errors: Thrown; every message starts 'zipnative: ' and names the remedy; err.code is the stable machine key, err.name/instanceof give the class.
sink.diagnostics: console.warn deduplicated per code per operation by default; onDiagnostic receives all; strict: true throws ZipError code ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC.
sink.cli: Every core call is wrapped by mapZipError(): error.code = the E_* class, error.zipCode = the ZIP_* code verbatim, plus entryName and code-specific detail when the core knows them. Diagnostics go to stderr as text (suppressed by --quiet) or travel in the --json envelope / report, deduplicated by (code, entryName) per run; --strict escalates the first one into ZIP_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC -> E_CHECK_FAILED (verify --strict prints the report, then E_VERIFY_FAILED).
